rationale: C22 is the clear drafting antecedent. It bears the identical title quoted by the child and created the nonpermanent appointment regime that the child’s proposed order sought to modify through a civil-service reserve and eventual absorption into permanent career positions. C23 is also closely related because it expressly creates permanent appointments and converts qualifying indefinite appointments under the C22 regime, but it is limited to the Post Office field service. C15 is a companion implementation letter for C22 and shares its personnel procedures, yet is less directly analogous to the child’s proposed legal machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Under present law, there is a restriction on the size of the permanent civil service so that nearly all appointments are made on an indefinite basis.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: all appointments in the executive branch of the Government shall be made on a non-permanent basis
shared_material.explanation: The child directly addresses the nonpermanent appointment system established by C22.

shared_material.child_excerpt: employees are appointed to this indefinite status from competitive civil service registers
shared_material.parent_excerpt: appointments and position changes in the competitive service shall be made in accordance with civil service laws, rules, and regulations
shared_material.explanation: Both preserve competitive civil-service procedures while assigning appointees a nonpermanent status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: would afford an orderly method for absorption of such appointees into the career civil service over a period of time as vacancies in the permanent service occur
shared_material.parent_excerpt: permanent appointments are authorized whenever, in unusual circumstances, the Civil Service Commission...determines that permanent appointments are in the interest of the Government
shared_material.explanation: The later proposal reworks C22’s exceptional permanent-appointment mechanism into a systematic route from indefinite to permanent service.
